title: Bridge Captain: Ludum Dare October Challenge 2012

contributors.contribution: Created the comic-book-style on-screen character artwork.
Wrote the bulk of the game's mission/story content in collaboration with Jamie.
Created the game's sound effects and music.

description: For the 2012 Ludum Dare October Challenge, I designed, built, released, and sold the first commercial version of Bridge Captain in under 30 days using my C.E.L.L. cross-platform game engine. The game combined starship bridge management, navigation, combat, resource control, crew interactions, and a complete branching story. I released a free desktop version through Ludum Dare and a paid Android version on Google Play, selling roughly 300 copies within the first few days before withdrawing the initial release to expand the project into a larger game.

sections.title: 30-Day Commercial Game Challenge
paragraphs: The Ludum Dare October Challenge was not a standard 48-hour jam. The goal was to create a game during October and take it all the way through release and actual sales.
I completed Bridge Captain and released it near the end of the month, around day 28 or 29.

sections.title: Built on C.E.L.L.
paragraphs: Bridge Captain was built using my C.E.L.L. cross-platform game engine.
The same codebase supported both the free desktop build and the Android commercial release.

sections.title: Starship Bridge Gameplay
paragraphs: The player acts as captain of a starship and interacts with multiple bridge systems and crew stations rather than controlling the ship through a single conventional game interface.

sections.title: Navigation & System Map
paragraphs: The game included navigation and system-map interfaces for moving between locations and managing mission travel.

sections.title: Ship Systems & Resource Management
paragraphs: Players managed ship resources and systems during missions.

sections.title: Combat
paragraphs: Ship-to-ship encounters used dedicated targeting and combat controls.
The player could select targets, aim weapons, manage charging and firing, and monitor ship condition during combat.

sections.title: Crew & Communications
paragraphs: Crew stations and communications were part of the game flow rather than simple decorative UI.
Mission information, dialogue, and story decisions were presented through the bridge and its crew interfaces.

sections.title: Branching Story
paragraphs: The challenge release contained a complete branching story rather than an unfinished story mode.
A first-time playthrough was approximately 40 minutes, while an experienced player who already knew the routes and decisions could complete it in roughly 20 minutes.

sections.title: Mission Writing
paragraphs: A long-time collaborator who had previously worked with me on the BlackBerry-era projects wrote the bulk of the mission content.
I collaborated on the story structure, gameplay integration, and mission implementation.

sections.title: Character Art
paragraphs: I created the game's UI, ship/interface artwork, and general visual presentation.
A collaborating comic-book artist created the illustrated on-screen character portraits.

sections.title: Music & Sound
paragraphs: A long-time audio collaborator created the game's sound effects and music.
The game did not use voice acting.

sections.title: Free Desktop Release
paragraphs: I released a desktop version for free through the Ludum Dare challenge portal as part of the October Challenge submission.

sections.title: Google Play Commercial Release
paragraphs: I also released Bridge Captain commercially on Google Play for Android.
The price was approximately $1, consistent with the challenge's goal of actually selling the finished game.

sections.title: Approximately 300 Paid Sales
paragraphs: The Android version sold roughly 300 paid copies within the first few days of release before I withdrew it from the store.

sections.title: Why I Withdrew the Initial Release
paragraphs: The initial game was complete, but early customer response made me realize that some players expected a much larger experience than the compact challenge release.
Rather than leave the smaller version on sale, I withdrew it and began expanding Bridge Captain into a substantially larger project.

sections.title: Beginning of a Larger Project
paragraphs: The October Challenge release became the foundation for later generations of Bridge Captain.
Those later versions expanded far beyond this initial release and are documented separately.

sections.title: Complete Release Pipeline
paragraphs: The challenge required more than building a prototype: I took the project through design, development, packaging, release, store publication, pricing, and actual commercial sales within the month.

historicalNotes: The legacy portfolio card called this 'Ludum Dare 30 Challenge (2012)'; the canonical framing is Ludum Dare October Challenge 2012.
This card represents only the original October 2012 Bridge Captain release generation. Later Bridge Captain generations should remain separate cards.
Jamie completed and released the project around day 28 or 29 of the October Challenge.
The game was built in C.E.L.L.
The desktop version was released free through the Ludum Dare portal.
The Android version was sold through Google Play.
Jamie remembers the Android price as approximately $1.
Approximately 300 paid copies sold within the first few days before Jamie withdrew the game.
The challenge release already contained a complete branching story.
First-time playthrough length was approximately 40 minutes.
An experienced player who knew the game could finish in roughly 20 minutes.
The legacy statement that Jamie pulled the game 'in order to complete the story mode' is inaccurate; the story was already complete.
The specific trigger Jamie remembers was a customer comment saying they had bought the game and booked off the weekend to play it.
That comment made Jamie realize some customers expected a substantially longer experience than the compact challenge release.
Keep the customer comment as private historical provenance rather than quoting it publicly in the portfolio.
Publicly frame the withdrawal as a response to early customer expectations and Jamie's decision to expand the project into a larger game.
Jamie created the game's UI, ship/interface graphics, and general artwork.
A comic-book artist created the illustrated on-screen character artwork.
A long-time collaborator from the earlier BlackBerry-era work wrote the bulk of the missions.
A long-time audio collaborator created the game's music and sound effects.
There was no voice acting in this release.
The broader Bridge Captain project later grew dramatically in scope and team size, but those facts belong to later-generation cards rather than this October Challenge card.
